note: Stop showing (REVEAL-6, REVEAL-22, X-3). Three scopes: one slot, every slot holding one document, or every slot of the session. A Stop carries NO epoch — it is never stale, never queued, never refused for state, and succeeds on an empty slot — so a stale number can never turn a narrowing into a refusal. There is no Retract in v1 (ED-16).

valid.name: stop showing this document, wherever it is live

invalid.name: a Stop carrying the reveal epoch
invalid.why: X-3, REVEAL-22: a narrowing is never stale and is never refused for state, so it carries no epoch to be stale against

invalid.name: Stop all carrying the reveal epoch
invalid.why: X-3: the same for the workspace indicator's Stop all, which is the panic button

invalid.name: a slot scope with no audience
invalid.why: a slot is named by its audience (AUD-8); without one there is nothing to clear

invalid.name: Stop all naming an audience
invalid.why: Stop all clears every slot of the session; an audience would make it a slot Stop wearing the wrong name

invalid.name: a document scope naming an audience as well
invalid.why: one scope per Stop: a document Stop clears every slot the document is live in (REVEAL-7), and mixing the two hides which rule applied

invalid.name: a scope this contract does not define
invalid.why: closed vocabulary: a Retract is the assistant's Phase 4, not a v1 scope (ED-16)

invalid.name: a Stop with no command id
invalid.why: a Stop is retried until acknowledged (REVEAL-16), so it must be recognisable as the same command
